tasks.short: Interview experts and develop instructional content.

steps.what: Read the brief card before this subject-matter interview.
Conduct the other research and develop the instructional content.

tasks.design: A brief card lists the topic, the expert's name, the one question, and the course the content is for. A programme colleague writes it when the interview is booked. The coordinator reads it, then still interviews the subject-matter experts and still develops the instructional content. If the card has no row, the coordinator uses the paper brief in the same step.
tasks.previous_blocker: The topic and the question lived in a programme folder the coordinator hunted before the interview.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper card with those four fields is enough. No new software is required.
tasks.still_hard: The expert's answer is unstructured. The coordinator still has to turn it into content.
tasks.human_edge: The coordinator hears what the expert will not put in a note, and chooses what belongs in the course.
tasks.altitude: The coordinator still interviews the expert and still writes the content. The card only shortens finding the brief.

reach.learn: Read a brief card, then still interview the expert and write the content.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the topic, the expert's name, the one question, and the course shortens the search when the row is there. The coordinator still interviews the expert and still writes the content. Model knowledge.

Admission, evaluating learning outcomes, assessing level, and test proctoring are high-risk under the cited annex. This interview develops instructional content and does none of those. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited annex.
Emotion recognition in education is prohibited under the cited article. This interview adds no emotion recognition. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited article.

assumptions: The programme colleague writes the brief card when the interview is booked.
Fields are the topic, the expert's name, the one question, and the course.
The card does not name a learner or a learner's results.
If the row is missing, the coordinator reads the paper brief inside s1.
Expert notes are written in s2, and s3 uses those notes.
There is no native system to configure and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because the programme colleague keeps the card, counted on the other line.
National staff-consultation rules for a monitoring tool are out of scope because this design adds none.
unknowns: Whether this firm already keeps a one-page brief for each expert interview.
research_questions: How often the expert or the course changes after the brief card is written.

incremental.description: No extra coordinator upkeep. The programme colleague keeps the brief card.
The programme colleague writes the brief card: topic, expert name, one question, and course.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The topic is often already known to this coordinator. The card saves the search only when the row is there and the course is not new.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Present course design and delivery recommendations.

steps.what: Read the option card before this course design recommendation.
Present the recommendations regarding course design, technology, and instruction delivery options.

tasks.design: An option card lists the course, the delivery option, and one constraint such as the room or the time. A programme colleague writes it from the last paper proposal. The coordinator reads it, then still presents the recommendations regarding course design and instruction delivery. If the card has no row, the coordinator uses the last paper proposal in the same step.
tasks.previous_blocker: The last delivery option sat in an old proposal the coordinator hunted before the meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper card with the course, the option, and one constraint is enough. No new software is required.
tasks.still_hard: Teachers can reject an option in the room. The coordinator still has to present it and hear them.
tasks.human_edge: The coordinator sees which option the teachers will actually use.
tasks.altitude: The coordinator still presents the recommendations. The card only shortens finding the last option.

reach.role: Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education
reach.task: Present a lesson option to colleagues
reach.learn: Read an option card, then still present the recommendation in the room.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the course, the delivery option, and one constraint shortens the search when the row is there. The coordinator still presents the recommendations. Model knowledge.

Admission, evaluating learning outcomes, assessing level, and test proctoring are high-risk under the cited annex. Presenting a delivery option does none of those. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited annex.

The cited guidance says schools should not put personal data in an AI tool, and should have a processor agreement and a DPIA. This option card names the course, the option, and one constraint. It holds no learner's results, and this design adds no such tool. Model knowledge of this design; the guidance is the cited page.

The spoken recommendations are made in s2, after the option points exist.
There is no native system to configure and no custom code.
Focal upkeep is zero because the programme colleague keeps the card, counted on the other line.

research_questions: How often teachers reject the pinned option in the room.

incremental.description: No extra coordinator upkeep. The programme colleague keeps the option card.

tasks.short: Give analytical support for training curricula.

steps.what: Read the standards card before this analytical support.
Provide analytical support for the design and development of training curricula, learning strategies, educational policies, or courseware standards.

tasks.design: A standards card lists the standard name, the course it covers, and the one requirement. A policy colleague writes it from the paper standard. The coordinator reads it, then still provides the analytical support for the curricula, the learning strategies, the educational policies, or the courseware standards. If the card has no row, the coordinator uses the paper standard in the same step.
tasks.previous_blocker: The requirement lived in a long policy the coordinator hunted before the analysis.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper card with the standard name, the course, and the one requirement is enough. No new software is required.
tasks.still_hard: The analysis is a judgement about whether the curriculum meets the requirement. The coordinator still writes it.
tasks.human_edge: The coordinator knows which requirement actually binds this course, and which line is only background.
tasks.altitude: The coordinator still writes the analysis. The card only shortens finding the standard.

reach.learn: Read a standards card, then still judge whether the material meets the requirement.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the standard name, the course, and the one requirement shortens the search when the row is there. The coordinator still writes the analysis. Model knowledge.

Admission, evaluating learning outcomes, assessing level, and test proctoring are high-risk under the cited annex. This analysis of a standard is none of those. Model knowledge of this design; the rule is the cited annex.

The cited guidance says schools should not put personal data in an AI tool, and should have a processor agreement and a DPIA. This standards card names the standard, the course, and one requirement. It holds no learner's results, and this design adds no such tool. Model knowledge of this design; the guidance is the cited page.

research_questions: How often the binding requirement changes after the standards card is written.

incremental.description: No extra coordinator upkeep. The policy colleague keeps the standards card.
The policy colleague writes the standards card: standard name, course, and one requirement.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The binding requirement is often already known. The card saves the search only when the row is there and the standard is not new.

steps.what: Read the cost card for the feasibility and the last cost of this course.
Recommend changes to curricula or delivery methods, based on information such as instructional effectiveness, current or future performance requirements, feasibility, and costs.

tasks.design: A cost card lists the course, the last cost, and one feasibility note. A finance colleague writes it when a quote is accepted. A teacher writes the effectiveness note beforehand: the course and one observation. The coordinator reads the cost card, then still recommends the changes from the effectiveness note, the performance requirements, the feasibility, and the costs. If the card has no row, the coordinator uses the paper quote in the same step.
tasks.previous_blocker: The last cost and the feasibility note lived in a quote folder the coordinator hunted before the recommendation.
tasks.enabler_now: A paper card with the course, the last cost, and one feasibility note is enough. No new software is required.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the change is worth the cost is a judgement. The coordinator still makes the recommendation.
tasks.human_edge: The coordinator weighs a teacher's observation against the cost and says what should change.
tasks.altitude: The coordinator still recommends the change. The card only shortens finding the last cost and the feasibility note.

reach.role: Elementary School Teachers, Except Special Education
reach.learn: Read a cost card and the teacher's note, then still recommend the change.

evidence.claim: A paper card with the course, the last cost, and one feasibility note shortens the search when the row is there. The coordinator still recommends the change. Model knowledge.
